chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abān, and al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Faḍālah, from Ibn Miskān, from Abū al-ʿAbbās, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said:

I asked him about the ghusl (ritual bath) of the deceased, and he said: Sit him up and press his stomach gently, then cleanse him of what comes out from pressing the stomach. Then lay him down, then wash him: begin with his right sides, and wash him with water and al-ḥuruḍ, then with water and camphor, then wash him with pure water, and place him in his shrouds.

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, may Allah have mercy on him, said: What this report contains in his statement, ‘Sit him up,’ agrees with the ʿĀmmah, and we do not act upon it. As for his statement, ‘Press him,’ it is possible that it is an indication of what is wiped over his stomach in the first two washings, not the third, as we have explained in our large book.

key_terms.أَكْفَانِهِ: his shrouds in which the deceased is wrapped
key_terms.اغْمِزْ بَطْنَهُ: press his stomach gently during preparation for washing
key_terms.الْغَسْلَتَيْنِ الْأَوَّلَتَيْنِ: the first two washings of the deceased
key_terms.الْمَاءِ الْقَرَاحِ: pure unmixed water used in the final washing
key_terms.الْمَاءِ وَالْحُرُضِ: water mixed with cleansing agent used in the first washing
key_terms.غُسْلِ الْمَيِّتِ: the ritual washing of the deceased
key_terms.مَاءٍ وَكَافُورٍ: water mixed with camphor used in the second washing

ai.seo_question: How is the deceased to be washed according to this hadith in al-Istibṣār?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the procedure of the ghusl (ritual bath) of the deceased, describing the sequence of washing and shrouding. It also includes Shaykh al-Ṭūsī’s note distinguishing between what is acted upon and what is not acted upon in the report according to Imami practice.
